Thereafter the following endovascular interventions were performed: thrombectomy and stenting of the right renal artery, superior mesenteric artery and distal aorta.

report.source_text: On reperfusion, there was massive swelling of both legs requiring several fasciotomies. The patient was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) where he remained intubated for 2 days. Second-look surgery was performed 24 hours after the first intervention and revealed viable abdominal organs except for the gallbladder, which was removed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old man with Crohn's disease presented with sudden-onset paraplegia, bilateral lower extremity pain, abdominal pain, and fecal incontinence. Physical examination revealed pale, cold, pulseless legs with flaccid paralysis, sensory loss from the T10 level (umbilicus), and absent femoral/distal pulses. Laboratory studies showed metabolic acidosis (pH 7.2, lactate 6.2 mmol/L) and acute kidney injury (creatinine 155 µmol/L). CT angiography confirmed extensive aortic thrombosis extending from the diaphragm to the aortic bifurcation without atherosclerosis. He underwent emergent open exploration revealing visceral ischemia, followed by endovascular thrombectomy and stenting of the right renal artery, superior mesenteric artery, and distal aorta. Postoperatively, he developed massive leg swelling requiring multiple fasciotomies, was intubated in the ICU for 2 days, and underwent second-look surgery at 24 hours showing viable abdominal organs except for the gallbladder which was removed. Hypercoagulability workup was negative. After 3.5 months of inpatient spinal rehabilitation, he regained some sensory function but remained wheelchair-dependent with permanent paraplegia.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Sudden onset paraplegia with bilateral leg pain, numbness, paralysis, and fecal incontinence

Physical examination findings consistent with acute bilateral lower extremity ischemia and spinal cord ischemia: pale, cold, numb legs with flaccid paralysis; absent femoral and distal pulses; sensory level at T10 (umbilicus); total loss of anal sphincter tone
Metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate (6.2 mmol/L) and acute kidney injury (creatinine 155 µmol/L) indicating tissue ischemia
CT angiography revealed aortic thrombosis extending from diaphragm to aortic bifurcation without atherosclerosis

Surgical intervention with open exploration confirmed extensive visceral ischemia and included endovascular thrombectomy and stenting of right renal artery, superior mesenteric artery, and distal aorta
Postoperative complications included massive leg swelling requiring fasciotomies and cholecystectomy due to gallbladder necrosis on second-look surgery
No underlying coagulation disorder identified despite thorough investigation
Permanent neurological deficit with partial sensory recovery but remained wheelchair-dependent after rehabilitation
